title: To Thy Blest Cross, O Christ, We Come
description: To Thy Blest Cross, O Christ, We Come in Tonic Solfa to DOMINUS REGIT ME, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to DOMINUS REGIT ME; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thy blest Cross, O Christ, we come, And fall-ing down a-dore Thee, And hum-bly_ make con-fes-sion_ full Of all our sins be-fore_ Thee.

lines: To Thy blest Cross, O Christ, we come,
Of all our sins before Thee.
For Thou Thyself art very God,
And freely cam'st to save us;
And in our flesh the fetters broke
With which our sins enslave us.
Therefore we own with grateful hearts
The joy the Saviour brought us,
Who came to earth, and in our sins
With love and pity sought us.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to DOMINUS REGIT ME by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
